title: Sixth Word Applying The Comparison Selling The Trust

questions.question: In the parable, who does the king stand for?
questions.answer: Allah, our Creator and Sustainer.

questions.question: What do the estates and tools stand for in a person’s life?
questions.answer: A person’s belongings, body, heart, spirit, and senses.

questions.question: Which person is the noble lieutenant in the parable?
questions.answer: The Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: What does the wise decree stand for?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the battle area stand for?
questions.answer: This changing world.

questions.question: What big worry do people feel when they see things changing and passing away?
questions.answer: They wonder if there is a way to keep things from being lost forever.

questions.question: What answer does the Qur’an give to that worry?
questions.answer: It says there is a good and easy way.

questions.question: What is that way?
questions.answer: To give the trust back to its real Owner.

questions.question: Who is the true Owner of the trust?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What kind of result comes from this trade?
questions.answer: It brings five benefits.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The nafs, meaning the selfish side of a person.

questions.question: What is the parable helping the reader see?
questions.answer: The truth.

questions.question: In the passage, what are some of the inner and outer gifts Allah gave people?
questions.answer: The eye, tongue, mind, imagination, heart, and spirit.

questions.question: Why is the world compared to a rough battlefield?
questions.answer: Because it keeps changing and nothing stays the same.

questions.question: What happens to things in this world according to the passage?
questions.answer: They pass away, break apart, and change.

questions.question: When people notice that things do not last, what question do they ask?
questions.answer: They ask if there is a way to make what they have lasting.

questions.question: From where does the answer come?
questions.answer: From the Qur’an.

questions.question: How is the way described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is beautiful and easy.

questions.question: What does it mean to sell the trust back?
questions.answer: It means giving what Allah gave us back to Him by using it for Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say this sale brings?
questions.answer: Five kinds of gain.

questions.question: Who is the Monarch of before and after all time in the parable?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Besides a person’s things, what other parts of a person are included in the trust?
questions.answer: The body, soul, heart, senses, mind, and imagination.

questions.question: Which two senses are named clearly in the passage?
questions.answer: The eye and the tongue.

questions.question: What is the job of the Messenger in the parable picture?
questions.answer: He is the noble messenger who brings the message.

questions.question: What book explains the trade mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the verse say Allah has taken from believers in exchange for Paradise?
questions.answer: Their selves and their property.

questions.question: Why does the world make people think deeply?
questions.answer: Because everything seems to slip away from them.

questions.question: What do people hope for when they ask about a way to preserve things?
questions.answer: They hope for a way to make them lasting.

questions.question: Is the path given in the passage shown as hard or simple?
questions.answer: It is shown as simple and good.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: Use Allah’s gifts in the way He wants, because they really belong to Him.

questions.question: In the story meaning, who gave people all their gifts?
questions.answer: Allah gave them.

questions.question: Name two parts of a person that are counted among these gifts.
questions.answer: The heart and the spirit.

questions.question: Name two abilities that are also part of the trust.
questions.answer: Intelligence and imagination.

questions.question: Who brings Allah’s message in this comparison?
questions.answer: The Noble Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: What writing gives the command about this trade?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why is life in this world like a stormy battle plain?
questions.answer: Because it is always moving, changing, and not staying fixed.

questions.question: What feeling comes when people see everything fading away?
questions.answer: They feel concern and want to know how to keep what matters.

questions.question: What is the beautiful way given in the passage?
questions.answer: To return the trust to its real Owner.

questions.question: What happens when someone does that?
questions.answer: The person receives five profits.

questions.question: In the parable, who is the real ruler over everything?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What are a person’s possessions in this passage?
questions.answer: What a person owns and also the gifts inside them, like body and senses.

questions.question: Are only outside things included in the trust, or inside gifts too?
questions.answer: Inside gifts too.

questions.question: Which holy person is shown by the lieutenant?
questions.answer: The Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: Which holy book is shown by the decree?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What verse idea is shared in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah buys from believers their selves and wealth, and gives Paradise.

questions.question: What does the changing world make every person realize?
questions.answer: That worldly things do not stay forever.

questions.question: After this realization, what do people begin to search for?
questions.answer: A way to keep things in a lasting form.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an say about such a way?
questions.answer: It says that way truly exists.

questions.question: What must a person do to take that way?
questions.answer: Give the trust back to Allah, its true Owner.

questions.question: Who is called the Creator and Sustainer in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What does the parable say the estate tools are like in our lives?
questions.answer: They are like our life gifts and abilities.

questions.question: What are some examples of those abilities?
questions.answer: Seeing, speaking, thinking, and imagining.

questions.question: Who is represented by the honored messenger in the parable?
questions.answer: The Prophet, the Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: What stands for the message that teaches this trade?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why is the world described like a place of battle and storms?
questions.answer: Because it keeps changing and things do not remain.

questions.question: What do people fear when they see everything changing?
questions.answer: They fear losing what is in their hands.

questions.question: What hopeful message do they then hear?
questions.answer: That there is a good and easy way to preserve what matters.

questions.question: How can a person preserve it in the way the passage teaches?
questions.answer: By returning the trust to Allah and using it for Him.

questions.question: How many profits does this bring?
questions.answer: Five.
